name: ANNetGPGPU
listed_description: A GPU (CUDA) based Artificial Neural Network library.
reason: No comparison against a recognizable baseline. The README claims only 'speed-ups by a factor of 100 ... for bigger networks (>256x256 nodes)' of its own CUDA self-organizing map (SOM) versus its own quad-core CPU/OpenMP SOM, plus Figure 1 (an image, no numbers) comparing training progress on a quad-core CPU and a GTX 570 in fixed time. Nothing against TensorFlow, PyTorch or any other library: README has no other numbers, no benchmark directory (root: src, CMakeLists, Doxyfile), issue search for benchmark, tensorflow, pytorch or speed returns 0 results. Last activity 2017; GitHub shows GPL-3.0 (awesome-cpp tag says LGPL), 113 stars.

name: cpp-mcp
listed_description: Lightweight C++ MCP (Model Context Protocol) SDK.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README has only a feature list and examples (HTTP/SSE and stdio transports, TLS, JSON-RPC 2.0); no benchmark directory (root: common, examples, include, src, test); issue search for benchmark, faster or performance returns 0 results. 'Lightweight' is a directional design claim with no footprint or speed numbers. MIT, 327 stars. The guessed TensorFlow or PyTorch baseline does not apply: it is a protocol SDK, not an ML library.

name: Duktape
listed_description: An embeddable JavaScript engine with compact footprint.
reason: No numeric speed or size win against a named baseline. Official docs say footprint matters more than speed: guide/intro.html 'This is more important than performance, as there are already several very fast engines', and guide/performance.html 'Overall Duktape performance should be similar to other interpreted languages' (only number: GCC -O2 with PGO about 20 percent faster than without PGO, a self comparison). The site's benchmarks.html is a plotly graph of Duktape's own commit history with no competitor engine; the index page footprint table (148 kB code, 78 kB RAM thumb default, 96 kB and 27 kB lowmem, 119 kB and 1.5 kB full lowmem) has no comparison column. The only third-party item found is an anecdote that Duktape was faster than MuJS (HN comment snippet, not a measurement); the QuickJS benchmark page (bellard.org/quickjs/bench.html, which lists Duktape) was EGRESS_BLOCKED, and search excerpts say QuickJS is faster than Duktape. MIT, 6.2k stars.

name: Evolving Objects
listed_description: A template-based, ANSI-C++ evolutionary computation library which helps you to write your own stochastic optimization algorithms insanely fast.
reason: No numbers reachable. The project page (eodev.sourceforge.net) and the SourceForge page (https://sourceforge.net/projects/eodev/) only say 'Fast running speed, thanks to C++ (sparing fitness call, functor-based calls)'; no benchmark or comparison, and the project is archived and merged into Paradiseo (last SourceForge update 2022-01-04; GPLv2 and LGPLv2). 'Insanely fast' in the lead means fast to write algorithms, not a speed claim. A third-party study exists, arXiv 2106.11919 'Speed Benchmarking of Genetic Programming Frameworks', which timed EO against ECJ, DEAP, TinyGP, KarooGP, GPlearn and TensorGP, but arxiv.org, deepai.org and paperswithcode were EGRESS_BLOCKED and search excerpts gave no EO timings (they say TensorGP is the fastest), so no EO-versus-baseline number could be read. Retry that paper if arXiv access opens up. The guessed TensorFlow or PyTorch baseline does not apply to this evolutionary computation library.

name: fastmcpp
listed_description: C++ port of the fastmcp Python library.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README says 'High-performance C++ implementation' and 'native performance' with no numbers; repo has no benchmark directory (root: include, src, tests, examples, CMakeLists); issue and PR search for benchmark, faster or performance finds only two CI PRs (#13 Windows CI split, #3 GitHub Actions) with no numbers. A web search for fastmcpp versus Python fastmcp found no measurement (other MCP benchmarks found do not include it). Directional claim only. Apache-2.0, 135 stars. The guessed TensorFlow or PyTorch baseline does not apply: it is an MCP protocol library; the natural baseline would be Python fastmcp.

name: hobbes
listed_description: A language and an embedded JIT compiler from Morgan Stanley.
reason: No numeric comparison against a recognizable baseline. README and docs (doc/en about, index, security, logging HLOG and hog pages) make design claims only (O(log r) match expressions, region allocation, 'efficient' native code, 'ultra-low latency') with no benchmark numbers; test/ has no perf or bench files; repo has no benchmark directory. Issues and PRs only carry self comparisons: issue #501 (match-table compilation about 5.8x slower with LLVM 16 than LLVM 8, a regression), PR #496 (about 7x faster match-table compiles versus the previous hobbes) and PR #578 (hobbes::cc construction about 20 percent faster). Web searches for talks or blogs with timing claims found none (habr.com article was EGRESS_BLOCKED, search excerpts show no numbers). Apache-2.0, 1.2k stars, active.
